findings.title: CI-gated shell suite still pins the pre-change env_vars shape and now fails
findings.detail: buildFullAccessLeadActionsMcpServerConfig now appends FLYWHEEL_LEAD_SUMMARY_ROLE / FLYWHEEL_LEAD_HAS_SUMMARY_DUTY / FLYWHEEL_SUMMARY_GRANULARITY to envVarNames, so codex-lead-tui-home.sh renders env_vars = ["BRIDGE_URL", "TEAMLEAD_API_TOKEN", "FLYWHEEL_LEAD_SUMMARY_ROLE", "FLYWHEEL_LEAD_HAS_SUMMARY_DUTY", "FLYWHEEL_SUMMARY_GRANULARITY"] (verified by running packages/teamlead/dist/bin/render-lead-actions-config.js at this HEAD). Two assertions in this suite still grep for the exact old strings: line 399 `env_vars = ["BRIDGE_URL", "TEAMLEAD_API_TOKEN"]` and line 431 `env_vars = ["DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN"]`. Both now miss because the closing bracket no longer follows the credential name. Measured at 8a72037: `bash packages/teamlead/scripts/__tests__/codex-lead-tui-home.test.sh` exits 1 with `Results: 62 passed, 2 failed` (`✗ full-access: env_vars missing`, `✗ FLY-2445 review: direct full-access home must use only DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`). This suite is a merge gate — .github/workflows/ci.yml:860 runs it — so the branch lands CI-red. The TS expectations in mcp-config.test.ts / codex-lead-runtime.test.ts were updated; this shell gate was missed. Fix: update both greps to the new exact env_vars text (bridge and direct variants), or derive them from the renderer output instead of a literal.

findings.title: Summary identity projection is incomplete: FLYWHEEL_SUMMARY_ASSIGNMENT_DIGEST still stripped
findings.detail: FULL_ACCESS_ENV_ALLOWLIST gains ROLE/DUTY/GRANULARITY but not FLYWHEEL_SUMMARY_ASSIGNMENT_DIGEST, which canonical_lead_identity_resolve exports alongside the other three (packages/teamlead/scripts/lib/canonical-lead-identity.sh:171-174) and which packages/flywheel-comm/src/commands/summary.ts:120-126 requires (`summary_assignment_digest_invalid`) for `flywheel-comm summary` create/update. Raya (recipient, duty=false) only needs the merge-authority tuple, so the reported `summary_merge_authority_required` incident is fixed. But growth/mufasa-lead is also a full-access Codex Lead and resolves to summaryRole=producer, hasSummaryDuty=true, summaryAssignmentDigest=643403c61d64… (verified against ~/.flywheel/projects.json via resolveLeadIdentity). From the Mufasa pane a summary submission now fails one step later — `summary_assignment_digest_invalid` instead of `summary_duty_required` — still blocked. Also note assertLeadIdentityIntegrity (packages/flywheel-comm/src/lead-lease.ts:2683-2699) compares the digest plus FLYWHEEL_LEAD_KEY/BACKEND/IDENTITY_DIGEST, none of which are allowlisted, so any Lead-write authorization from a full-access Codex pane still denies. Either add the digest (and say why the rest are deliberately withheld) or state in the milestone that only the Raya recipient path is covered.

findings.title: Non-authoritative StateStore mirror can fail the already-committed batch ACK
findings.detail: The mirror loop runs unguarded after queue.ackBatchByRecipient has already committed the mailbox ACK. If getLeadEventBySeq or markSummaryAbsorptionAcked throws (StateStore busy/locked/corrupt), handle() throws, and LeadInboxLoop (packages/teamlead/src/bridge/lead-inbox-loop.ts:266-289) records a bridge delivery failure, retries, and after maxProtocolAttempts dead-letters the row and fires onProtocolQuarantine. Concrete scenario: teamlead.db hits SQLITE_BUSY during a lead-restart herd — the batch is genuinely ACKed in CommDB, yet the Lead's ack_batch receipt is repeatedly replayed and finally quarantined with an alert, purely because a mirror the code itself documents as non-canonical could not be written. The comment on markSummaryAbsorptionAcked says it only mirrors the canonical mailbox receipt, so its criticality should be lower than the thing it mirrors: wrap the loop in try/catch + console.warn (the duplicate-receipt replay path already covers the repair case), or move it inside the same CommDB effect so it cannot half-fail.

findings.title: Allowlist gains two names the Claude pane never injects, contradicting its own SSOT comment
findings.detail: FULL_ACCESS_ENV_ALLOWLIST is documented (codex-lead-runtime.ts:391-401) as 'EXACTLY the names claude-lead.sh injects into a Claude pane' plus the gh-auth set, and the env-diff test only asserts result ⊆ allowlist, so nothing catches drift. FLYWHEEL_LEAD_CROSS_DEPT_CHANNEL_IDS and FLYWHEEL_LEAD_ACTIONS_CHANNEL_ALIASES appear nowhere in claude-lead.sh's `env_args` block (packages/teamlead/scripts/claude-lead.sh:2098-2231), so the comment is now false. Neither name has an in-pane consumer either: flywheel-comm never reads them, and the lead_actions MCP child already receives cross-dept ids as a literal in its config.toml `env` table (mcp-config.ts:165), derived from config.crossDeptChannelIds rather than from the daemon env. Values are non-secret channel ids so there is no disclosure, but the SSOT comment should be corrected and the rationale for the two extra names recorded — otherwise the next reader treats the allowlist as a verified Claude-pane mirror when it no longer is.

findings.title: Canonical delivery id re-derived inline instead of via canonicalLeadEventDeliveryId
findings.detail: The binding check hardcodes `lead_event:${event.lead_id}:${event.event_id}`, while the producer (lead-event-queue.ts:8-13) builds it as `envelope.eventId?.trim() || \`seq:${envelope.seq}\``. For a journal row whose event_id is empty or whitespace-padded, the real mailbox delivery_id is `lead_event:<lead>:seq:<n>` (or the trimmed form) and this comparison never matches, so the mirror silently skips a legitimate receipt. summary_absorption_round always carries a non-empty roundId, so this is latent today, but the two derivations can drift independently. Call canonicalLeadEventDeliveryId(leadEventEnvelopeFromJournalRow(event)) — or export a small shared helper — so there is one definition.

findings.title: Summary identity forwarded into the lead_actions MCP child that never reads it
findings.detail: The three summary names are appended to envVarNames unconditionally, so they are forwarded into the lead_actions MCP child and pinned into the exact-match §10 gate (assertFullAccessLeadActionsConfigGate compares env_vars element-by-element). Nothing under packages/teamlead/src/lead-backends/codex/lead-actions/ reads FLYWHEEL_LEAD_SUMMARY_ROLE / FLYWHEEL_LEAD_HAS_SUMMARY_DUTY / FLYWHEEL_SUMMARY_GRANULARITY (parseLeadActionsConfig ignores them), and runner-actions.ts spawns nothing from env. The actual fix for the production incident is the FULL_ACCESS_ENV_ALLOWLIST change, which feeds the pane shell where flywheel-comm runs. Concretely this makes a config gate stricter for values nobody consumes — it is what broke the CI shell suite above. Consider dropping the envVarNames half, or document the intended future consumer.
